Wait for the row's status pill to update: Verified, Failed, or Timeout.

checks.note: true only if a Timeout pill exists

claims.finding: There is no Timeout pill. The pill shows '✅ Verified', '⏳ Pending', '⏳ Pending Approval', '📋 Manual Required', '✗ Failed', and any other status (including 'timeout') falls through to '⚠ Expired' (frontend/src/pages/BillingAuthPage.tsx:6110-6134). A row whose legacy verified flag is still true shows Verified regardless of status (frontend/src/utils/insuranceStatus.ts:10-14).
claims.proposed_text: Wait for the row's status pill to update: Verified, Failed, Pending, Pending Approval, Manual Required, or Expired (a timed-out check shows Expired unless the row was already verified).
claims.reason: There is no Timeout pill; a timed-out row shows Expired (or Verified). Replaced by elig-07b.

claims.reason: The button is "View Response" and shows only on verified, non-manual rows. Replaced by elig-08b.

You can re-verify at any time. The most recent attempt wins on the record — including a fresh Failed or Timeout, which correctly replaces a stale Verified.

checks.note: true only if the verified flag is not held back on transport failures

claims.finding: The status column takes the latest attempt, but on a transport failure (timeout / 5xx) the legacy verified flag is left as it was (verifyInsuranceCore.ts:352-356), and the screen treats verified=true as Verified (frontend/src/utils/insuranceStatus.ts:13). So a fresh timeout does NOT replace a stale Verified on screen; only a payer answer (active or not) does.
claims.proposed_text: You can re-verify at any time. A payer answer always replaces the previous result, including an inactive answer replacing an old Verified. A timeout records the attempt but keeps an earlier verification.
claims.reason: A timeout leaves the old verified flag, so it does not replace a stale Verified on screen. Replaced by elig-09b.

claims.claim: You can re-verify at any time. A payer answer always replaces the previous result, including an inactive answer replacing an old Verified. A timeout records the attempt but keeps an earlier verification.
Plan status — Medipyxis checks whether any plan status the payer returns says "active". This is the authoritative "is coverage active today" signal.
claims.reason: It reads the numeric EB01 status code (1-5, 11), with an exact-label fallback — not a 'says active' text match (eligibilityStatus.ts:26-85). The behavior described holds.

claims.claim: Verified — Stedi returned a response AND the payer reports at least one active plan. Failed — Stedi returned a response but no active plan, OR any other error that is not a timeout.
Timeout — Stedi timed out. An earlier verification is preserved — a connection failure does not erase a prior real verification.
Timeout — the pill shows Expired.

On every 270/271 round trip, Medipyxis saves: Verification status, Last verified (date and time of this attempt), Raw 271 (only when active), Copay, deductible, deductible met, coinsurance %, out-of-pocket max, out-of-pocket met, and Notes.
claims.reason: Benefit columns are written only when the 271 carried that value; otherwise the previous value is kept.

claims.claim: Notes — Summary — plan name, payer, and any error text.
The raw 271 is saved only when coverage is active, so the response view never shows an inactive or terminated plan as active coverage.

Medipyxis reads the X12 271 EB01 code letter (not the free-text benefit name): A coinsurance %, B copay, C deductible (or deductible met for a remaining/met/used variant), G out-of-pocket max (or out-of-pocket met for the remaining variant).
claims.reason: The remaining/met variant is detected from the benefit name text, and 'met' is computed as amount minus remaining. Entries with no EB01 code fall back to name matching (parseBenefits.ts:209-235).

claims.claim: Within a benefit type, entries are ranked: individual coverage outranks family, in-network outranks out-of-network, and service type 30 outranks others. The highest-ranked line wins.
When the payer sends a Co-Payment (EB01 B) line, that is always the copay Medipyxis uses. Other copay-like text from a non-standard payer cannot override it.
A verified row unblocks pre-service checks in the Work Queue, feeds copay/deductible into the biller-facing claim summary, and preserves the exact 271 for audit.

checks.note: true only if the Work Queue reads the verification result

claims.finding: No billing Work Queue component reads verification_status or isInsuranceVerified (frontend/src/components/billing has no hit), and the claim editor initialises copay_amount to null rather than reading the verified copay (frontend/src/pages/NewBillingSubmitPage.tsx:2450). Only the 271-preserved part holds (verifyInsuranceCore.ts:358-369).
claims.proposed_text: A verified row keeps the exact 271 so you can open it with View Response.
claims.reason: No Work Queue check reads the verification, and the claim editor does not read the verified copay. Replaced by elig-19b.

claims.claim: A verified row keeps the exact 271 so you can open it with View Response.

Status flips Verified → Failed on re-verify → coverage really did lapse, OR the member ID / DOB is mistyped. Compare the row's notes to the raw 271.
claims.reason: A payer answer with no active plan sets verified=false and status failed. Note the raw 271 is not saved for a failed check (elig-15), so only the notes can be compared.

claims.claim: Copay is $0.00 but the payer's card shows a copay → The 271 either had no Co-Payment (EB01 B) line or listed only family coverage.

checks.note: true only if a family-only B line is ignored

claims.finding: A family-only Co-Payment line is still used: ranking only orders candidates, it never drops one, so a lone family B line becomes the copay (backend/supabase/functions/verify-insurance/parseBenefits.ts:182-192). When no copay is found the column is left unchanged rather than set to $0 (verifyInsuranceCore.ts:371).
claims.proposed_text: Copay is blank or old but the payer's card shows a copay → the 271 had no Co-Payment (EB01 B) line. Open View Response and read the benefits.
claims.reason: A family-only copay line is still used, and a missing copay leaves the old value rather than $0. Replaced by elig-24b.
